SMTO-MAN-0003 — This Manual link isn't in a form SMTO recognizes

GUID: 4de27961-e07f-4876-a964-5f713f5fe158
Slug: manual-document-invalid
Domain: MAN · Subsystem: man

What happened

  • The page name in this Manual link uses characters or a length the Manual doesn't allow, so it couldn't look the page up. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Manual from the navigation menu and find the page with the Search manual box or the page list. Links the Manual creates itself always use a valid page name.
  2. If you copied the link from somewhere, check it wasn't cut off or changed. Page names use only lowercase letters, numbers and dashes. Capital letters, spaces or other symbols make the page name invalid.
  3. If every Manual page fails to open, tell the person who manages SMTO. A damaged Manual installation, for example two pages with the same name, stops the Manual from loading its pages.

What success looks like

  • The page opens, and its link shows a page name made only of lowercase letters, numbers and dashes.

If it still fails

  • Copy the link and the error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit the Manual's files yourself to fix it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Manual ID validation failed: the requested document ID is not 1-120 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens starting with a letter or digit (HTTP 400), or corpus construction rejected duplicate document IDs, an unknown authority, inconsistent source classification or headings, or duplicate section references.

What this means

  • Manual ID validation rejects unsupported syntax, or corpus construction finds duplicate identities, inconsistent source authority/headings or duplicate section references. Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.

Why this can happen

  • Manual ID validation rejects unsupported syntax, or corpus construction finds duplicate identities, inconsistent source authority/headings or duplicate section references.

How to diagnose it

  • Separate a malformed user URL from an invalid installed corpus; only the latter needs build/content repair.

How to fix it

  • For a 400 response, use a valid lowercase document ID from GET /api/manual/catalog. If corpus construction raised ValueError in manual.corpus._snapshot, repair or reinstall the installed Manual content so document IDs and section references are unique and front-matter headings match the document body.
  • Use a current canonical link; if corpus construction reports conflicting document metadata, repair the installed Manual content.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Valid references resolve against a corpus with unique consistent document and section identities.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
